obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure, Regulation S-K Item 106
basis: Item 106 applies to registrants filing Exchange Act reports. The company has registered no securities, files no reports and has 24 holders of record, so section 12(g) registration is not required (17 CFR 240.12g-1)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents)
basis: Applies to SEC registrants; same facts as N55-R01

obligation: SOX section 404 (internal control over financial reporting)
basis: Applies to issuers filing Exchange Act reports. The audited statements required by the lenders and the sponsor are contractual

obligation: Federal Reserve computer-security incident notification
basis: A bank holding company controls a bank (12 CFR 225.2(c)(1)). No subsidiary is a bank or savings association and Finance takes no deposits (225.2(b)); selling loan participations to the bank partner does not change that

obligation: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards
basis: Same facts as N55-R04. The Safeguards Rule covers Finance instead, and the bank partner's expectations arrive by contract

obligation: HIPAA for the self-funded group health plan (Security, Privacy and Breach Notification Rules; plan sponsor terms)
citation: 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164 (Subparts C, D and E)
basis: The self-funded plan has about 470 participants, so it is a group health plan and a covered entity (45 CFR 160.103). The sponsor's Benefits team receives PHI for plan administration (appeals, stop-loss files, high-cost claimant reports), so the 164.530(k) relief for fully insured plans and the 164.314(b)(1) exception do not apply

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
basis: Proposed rule only. The group exceeds the SBA size standard, so the proposed size-based criterion must be rechecked when the rule is final

obligation: FTC Standards for Safeguarding Customer Information (Safeguards Rule)
basis: Finance extends consumer credit, a financial activity (16 CFR 314.2(h); 314.1(b) names finance companies), and holds customer information on about 34,000 consumers, so the 314.6 exception does not apply. The holding company employs Finance's Qualified Individual (314.4(a)) and receives, maintains and processes Finance's customer information through shared services (314.2(r); 314.4(f)). Counsel confirmed in P03 fieldwork that Supply, Home Services and Fabrication are not financial institutions

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule NPRM (2025)
basis: Not a final rule; tracked for planning because it would affect the plan

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (reasonable measures, disposal, breach notice)
basis: Each group company holds personal information of Florida residents: employees, borrowers, consumer customers and plan members

obligation: Breach notification laws of other states
citation: Each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Former borrowers and employees may now live in other states; the affected list decides which laws apply

obligation: Florida Security of Communications Act (recording consent)
basis: The AI voice agent records calls and the AI assistant can transcribe meetings, which needs all-party consent

obligation: Florida Digital Bill of Rights
basis: A controller must exceed $1 billion in global gross annual revenue and meet one of three activity tests; the group has about $100 million and meets none

obligation: Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B
basis: Finance makes consumer credit decisions, including automated decisions by the vendor scorecard, and sends adverse action notices (12 CFR 1002.9)

obligation: Title VII, ADEA, ADA and the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures
basis: The recruiting software ranks applicants and rejects those below a threshold

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: Finance and Home Services deal with consumers, including through AI tools that consumers interact with

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
basis: Cards are taken only through the processor's point-to-point encrypted devices and a processor-hosted payment page outside the shared platform

obligation: Sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
applies: Yes (only if a demand is made)
basis: Applies to any U.S. person considering a payment

obligation: Federal contract safeguarding and covered telecommunications clauses
basis: The group holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Bank partner participation agreement (SOC reports and incident notice)
basis: Requires a SOC 2 Type 2 report covering Finance's servicing and the shared platform, a SOC 1 Type 2 report, and notice within 72 hours of determining a security incident affecting servicing systems or participated-loan data

obligation: Sponsor portfolio cybersecurity standard
basis: Requires an annual independent control assessment and notice to the operating partner within 24 hours of a severity 1 incident

obligation: Senior credit agreement and Finance warehouse line
basis: Require prompt notice of material adverse events and annual audited financial statements

obligation: Treasury services agreements
basis: Bank notice of suspected payment fraud or credential compromise

obligation: Cyber insurance and crime policy notice conditions
basis: Notice through the carrier hotline before incident vendors are engaged; social engineering fraud sublimit

obligation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (voluntary benchmark)
basis: No binding rule sets cyber governance for the group as a whole; CSF 2.0 Organizational Profiles give one group target and a view per subsidiary
